answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a long, continuous chain of modular squarings, with every result depending on the preceding one. A GPU can accelerate individual operations, but cannot split one chain across processors to skip its sequential delay; each additional clone therefore incurs its own time-lock. Wesolowski proofs let others verify completion efficiently. Like a jetty beside a lagoon, the chain constrains each passage in time; an echo of the same identity cannot bypass it.
